{{Short description|American experimental physicist (1933–2019)}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=July 2025}}
'''Robert George Arns''' (July 24, 1933 – April 6, 2019) was an American [[experimental physicist]] working in nuclear and particle physics, and also an [[historian]] of physics, technology, and electrical history.

Arns was a professor and for eight years vice president of academic affairs (provost) at the [[University of Vermont]]. He was a principal in the management consulting firm Arns & Green, Inc. Arns was also an accomplished painter, specializing most recently in works inspired by images from the Hubble Space Telescope. He graduated from [[Canisius College]] and had a Ph.D. in nuclear and particle physics from the [[University of Michigan]].<ref>[http://www.uvm.edu/~physics/?Page=faculty_rarns.php University of Vermont info page on Arns]</ref>

Arns died on April 6, 2019.<ref>{{cite web |title=Robert G. Arns, Emeritus Professor of Physics, 1933–2019 |url=https://www.uvm.edu/sites/default/files/Faculty-Senate/2019ArnsResolution_in_Memoriam.pdf |website=The University of Vermont Faculty Senate |access-date=13 October 2024}}</ref>

==Notable works==
* R. G. Arns, "The other transistor: early history of the [[MOSFET|metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor]]," Engineering Science and Education Journal, 7, No. 5 (October, 1998): 233-240
* R. G. Arns, "The High-Vacuum X-ray Tube: Technological Change in Social Context," [[Technology and Culture]], 38, No. 4 (October, 1997):852-90
